items.title: 7.1.3 Displacement, Average Velocity and Acceleration (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: PDF 221-222 (book p. 219-220): signs for direction, average velocity and speed, Recall! box, Examples 1-2 (both printed as 'Example 2'), instantaneous velocity and speed, acceleration, units

blocks.text: Pichle do sabaqon mein humne scalars aur vectors ka farq samjha. Ab un ko istemal karne ki baari hai. Is sabaq mein teen bari cheezein aayengi: average velocity aur average speed, instantaneous (usi lamhe ki) velocity aur speed, aur acceleration. Aur yahin pehli dafa aap dekhenge ke derivative motion mein kaise kaam aata hai.
Kitab kehti hai: jab koi particle rectilinear motion karta hai, to us ka displacement, velocity aur acceleration sirf do mein se ek direction rakh sakte hain, dono line of motion ke saath.
Aise mein hum direction dikhane ke liye teer (arrow) ya doosre vector symbols istemal nahin karte; balke positive aur negative signs se direction batate hain:

items: Line ke saath ek direction ko positive maana jata hai.
Ulti direction ko negative maana jata hai.

blocks.text: Is se rectilinear motion mein displacement, velocity aur acceleration ko likhna aasaan ho jata hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Number line ko yaad kijiye. Us par chalne wala particle sirf daayen (right) ya baayen (left) ja sakta hai, is liye sirf ek sign kaafi hai direction batane ke liye. Kaun si taraf positive kehni hai, yeh aap ki marzi hai (east, upar, school ki taraf...), lekin ek dafa chun li to poore sawal mein wahi rakhni hai. Beech mein badal di to jawab ghalat ho jayega.
Average Velocity
Kitab ki definition: kisi cheez ki average velocity (\(v\)) kul displacement ko kul time se divide karne se milti hai:

blocks.latex: v_{avg} = \text{Average velocity} = \dfrac{\text{Total displacement}}{\text{Total Time}} = \dfrac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}
blocks.text_alt: v average equals average velocity equals total displacement over total time equals delta x over delta t

blocks.text: Average Speed
Average speed kul tay kiye gaye distance ko kul time se divide karne se milti hai:

blocks.text_alt: average speed equals total distance travelled over total time

blocks.title: Recall!
blocks.text:
Jab koi body chal kar wapas apni starting position (shuru wali jagah) par aa jaye:
Displacement \(= 0\)
Distance \(\ne 0\)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ke Recall! box mein "a body goes and come back starting position" likha hai (grammar theek nahin), aur "Distance" aur "0" ke beech koi nishan (sign) chhapa hi nahin. Sahi baat yeh hai: jab body wapas apni starting position par aa jaye to Displacement \(= 0\), lekin Distance \(\ne 0\), kyun ke distance poore raaste ki lambai hai jo zero nahin hoti. Upar humne sahi shakal likhi hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(\Delta x\) ("delta x" parhte hain) ka matlab hai "\(x\) mein tabdeeli" = final position \(-\) initial position. Isi tarah \(\Delta t\) = final time \(-\) initial time.
Average velocity displacement se banti hai, is liye negative ya zero bhi ho sakti hai. Average speed distance se banti hai, is liye kabhi negative nahin hoti. Jab particle kabhi wapas na mude to dono ka size barabar hota hai; wapas mude to average speed bari hoti hai.
Misaal: aap school gaye aur wapas ghar aa gaye. Average velocity zero, kyun ke displacement zero hai. Lekin average speed zero nahin, kyun ke aap ne raasta to tay kiya!

blocks.title: Numbering note (ours)
blocks.text: Kitab mein Example 1 chhapa hi nahin, aur in do safhon par "Example 2" ka number do dafa chhapa hai: pehli dafa east aur phir west chalne wale aadmi ke liye, doosri dafa \(x(t) = t^{3} - 6t^{2}\) wale particle ke liye. Hum ne pehli misaal ko Example 1 aur doosri ko Example 2 likha hai. Example 3 se aage kitab ke chhape hue number hi rakhe hain, taa ke baad wali har misaal kitab mein usi number se mil jaye.
Ab pehli misaal. Is mein dono formulas saath saath lagenge, taa ke aap farq khud dekh sakein.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.problem: A man walks 100 meters east in 2 minutes, then turns around and walks 60 meters west in 1 minute. Find his speed and velocity.
steps:
Diya gaya: aadmi 2 minute mein 100 m east chala, phir mud kar 1 minute mein 60 m west chala.
Maloom karna: poore safar ki average speed aur average velocity.
Tareeqa: sab se pehle dekhte hain ke sawal kya maang raha hai: speed aur velocity, dono. Average speed = kul distance / kul time (direction ki parwah nahin). Average velocity = kul displacement / kul time (direction sign ke saath). "Average" is liye ke humein har lamhe ki raftaar nahin, sirf kul hisaab maloom hai.

Step 1: Kul distance aur kul time
\[\text{Total distance} = 100 + 60\]
\[= 160\ \text{meters}\]
\[\text{Total time} = 2 + 1 = 3\ \text{minutes}\]
Kyun: distance scalar hai, is liye raaste ke dono tukre seedhe jama ho jate hain, chahe kisi bhi taraf hon.

Step 2: Average speed
\[\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{\text{Total distance travelled}}{\text{Total Time}}\]
\[= \dfrac{160}{3}\]
\[= 53.3\ \text{meters/min}\]
Kyun: yeh average speed ki definition hai. \(\frac{160}{3} = 53.33...\) ko ek decimal tak likha hai.

Step 3: Signs ke saath displacements
East ko positive aur west ko negative maan lete hain:
\[x_{1} = 100\ \text{meters}\]
\[x_{2} = -60\ \text{meters}\]
\[\text{Total displacement} = x_{1} + x_{2}\]
\[= 100 - 60 = 40\ \text{meters}\]
Kyun: displacement vector hai; seedhi line par us ki direction sign se dikhti hai. West wala safar east wale safar ka kuch hissa "kaat" deta hai. Aakhir mein aadmi apni shuru wali jagah se 40 m east mein khada hai.
Dhyan dein: yahan bohat se students 60 ko bhi plus kar dete hain. Displacement mein ulti taraf ka safar hamesha minus sign ke saath aata hai.

Step 4: Average velocity
\[v_{avg} = \dfrac{\text{Total displacement}}{\text{Total Time}}\]
\[= \dfrac{40}{3}\]
\[= 13.33\ \text{meters/min (eastward)}\]
Kyun: average velocity ki definition. Jawab positive hai, is liye direction positive yani east hai. Velocity ke jawab ke saath direction likhna na bhoolein.

Tasdeeq:
Average velocity ki magnitude kabhi average speed se zyada nahin ho sakti, kyun ke \(|\text{displacement}| \le \text{distance}\). Yahan \(13.33 \le 53.3\), theek hai. Dono mein farq is liye hai ke aadmi beech mein wapas mura; agar woh sirf east chalta rehta to dono barabar hotin.
blocks.answer: Average speed \(= \frac{160}{3} \approx 53.3\) meters/min; average velocity \(= \frac{40}{3} \approx 13.33\) meters/min east ki taraf.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Agar yahi aadmi 100 m east chalne ke baad poore 100 m wapas west aa jata (kul time phir bhi 3 minute), to average velocity aur average speed kya hoti?
Displacement \(= 100 - 100 = 0\), is liye average velocity \(= \frac{0}{3} = 0\). Distance \(= 100 + 100 = 200\) m, is liye average speed \(= \frac{200}{3} \approx 66.7\) m/min. Yeh bilkul Recall! box wali baat hai: wapas apni jagah aa jao to displacement zero, magar distance zero nahin.

Yahan tak humne poore safar ka "average" dekha. Lekin average se yeh pata nahin chalta ke kisi khaas lamhe par aadmi kitni tezi se chal raha tha. Shayad pehle minute mein tez chala ho aur doosre mein aahista. Har lamhe ki velocity ke liye humein naya tool chahiye: derivative. Yahin se calculus kinematics mein dakhil hota hai.
Instantaneous Velocity

Kitab ki definition: instantaneous velocity kisi khaas lamhe (instant) par time ke lehaaz se displacement ka rate of change hai. Agar \(x(t)\) kisi bhi waqt \(t\) par particle ka displacement ho, to waqt \(t\) par instantaneous velocity \(v(t)\) yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: v of t equals d x by d t

blocks.text: Instantaneous Speed
Instantaneous speed instantaneous velocity ki magnitude hai:

blocks.text_alt: instantaneous speed equals modulus of v of t equals modulus of d x by d t

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yahan derivative kyun aaya? Average velocity ek waqfe (interval) par \(\frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}\) hai. Ab is waqfe ko kisi ek lamhe ke ird gird chhota, aur chhota, aur chhota karte jaiye. Jab \(\Delta t \to 0\) ho, to \(\frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}\) ki limit bilkul derivative \(\frac{dx}{dt}\) hai. Yaani instantaneous velocity = "bohat hi chhote waqt ki average velocity".
Roz ki misaal: motorway par aap ne 2 ghante mein 200 km tay kiye, to average speed 100 km/h hai. Magar kisi khaas lamhe par speedometer 120 bhi dikha sakta tha aur 80 bhi. Speedometer jo dikhata hai woh instantaneous speed hai.
\(v(t)\) ka sign direction batata hai: \(v > 0\) to positive direction mein, \(v < 0\) to negative direction mein, aur \(v = 0\) to us lamhe particle ruka hua hai (yahin particle wapas mud sakta hai).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar \(x(t) = 5t\) ho to velocity kya hai? \(v = \frac{d}{dt}(5t) = 5\) m/s, har waqt ek jaisi. Yaani jab position \(t\) ka seedha (linear) function ho to velocity constant hoti hai. Agle sabaq (7.1.4) mein yehi baat graph par seedhi line ki shakal mein nazar aayegi.

Ab Example 2 ki taraf chalte hain. Yahan sawal ka andaaz badal gaya hai: ab humein kul distance aur kul time nahin diye, balke position ka formula diya hai jo har lamhe ki position batata hai. Jab bhi sawal mein "at any time \(t\)" ya "at \(t = 1\)" jaise lafz aayein, samajh jaiye ke instantaneous velocity maangi ja rahi hai, aur iska matlab hai derivative. Teen kaam karne hain: pehle derivative le kar \(v(t)\) banana, phir absolute value se speed, aur aakhir mein \(t = 1\) rakh kar numbers nikaalna.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.problem: Let \(x(t) = t^{3} - 6t^{2}\) be the position of a particle moving along a straight line at any time \(t\), where \(x\) is in meters and \(t\) is in seconds. Find the velocity and the speed of the particle at any time \(t\) and at \(t = 1\) second.
steps:
Diya gaya: position \(x(t) = t^{3} - 6t^{2}\) (meters aur seconds mein).
Maloom karna: kisi bhi waqt \(t\) par velocity aur speed, aur phir \(t = 1\) s par.
Tareeqa: yahan position waqt ka function di hui hai, is liye instantaneous velocity ke liye derivative lenge: \(v(t) = \frac{dx}{dt}\). Speed us ki absolute value \(|v(t)|\) hai. Average wala formula yahan nahin lagega, kyun ke "at any time" yani har lamhe ki baat ho rahi hai.

Step 1: \(t\) ke lehaaz se differentiate karein
\[\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 3t^{2} - 12t\]
Kyun: power rule \(\frac{d}{dt}(t^{n}) = nt^{n-1}\): \(\frac{d}{dt}(t^{3}) = 3t^{2}\) aur \(\frac{d}{dt}(6t^{2}) = 6 \cdot 2t = 12t\).

Step 2: Kisi bhi waqt \(t\) par velocity aur speed
\[v(t) = 3t^{2} - 12t \quad \text{...(1)}\]
\[\text{Speed} = |v(t)| = |3t^{2} - 12t| \quad \text{...(2)}\]
Kyun: velocity \(\frac{dx}{dt}\) hai; speed velocity ki magnitude hai, is liye absolute value (modulus) lagaya.

Step 3: (1) aur (2) mein \(t = 1\) rakhein
\[v(1) = 3(1)^{2} - 12(1)\]
\[= 3 - 12 = -9\ \text{meter/second}\]
\[\text{Speed} = |v(1)| = |-9| = 9\ \text{m/s}\]
Kyun: Step 2 ke formulas mein \(t = 1\) rakha. Minus sign ka matlab hai ke \(t = 1\) s par particle negative direction mein chal raha hai. Speed ka koi sign nahin hota, is liye 9 m/s.
Dhyan dein: velocity ka jawab \(-9\) hai, \(9\) nahin. Minus ko "ghalti" samajh kar hata dena sab se aam ghalti hai; woh direction ki maloomat hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(t = 1\) par \(x = 1 - 6 = -5\) m; \(t = 1.01\) par \(x = 1.030301 - 6.1206 = -5.090299\) m. Sirf 0.01 s mein position taqreeban \(-0.09\) m badli, yani taqreeban \(\frac{-0.09}{0.01} = -9\) m/s. Bilkul wahi jo derivative ne diya!

blocks.text: Velocity ke baad agla qudrati sawal yeh hai: kya velocity khud badal rahi hai? Example 2 mein \(v(t) = 3t^{2} - 12t\) har lamhe badalti hai: \(t = 1\) par \(-9\), \(t = 2\) par \(-12\), \(t = 5\) par \(15\). Velocity ke badalne ki raftaar ko naam dete hain: acceleration. Jis tarah velocity position ka derivative thi, usi tarah acceleration velocity ka derivative hai. Pattern yaad rakhiye: position se velocity, velocity se acceleration, har qadam par ek derivative.
Acceleration
Kitab ki definition: time ke lehaaz se velocity ke rate of change ko acceleration kehte hain. Agar \(v(t)\) kisi bhi waqt \(t\) par particle ki velocity ho, to us ka acceleration \(a(t)\) yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: a of t equals d v by d t

blocks.text: Kyun ke \(v = \frac{dx}{dt}\), is liye upar wali expression yun bhi likhi ja sakti hai:

blocks.text_alt: a of t equals d v by d t equals d by d t of d x by d t equals second derivative of x with respect to t

blocks.text: Yaani acceleration position ka second derivative (do dafa derivative) hai. Ab agar velocity \(v\) displacement \(x\) ka function di ho (time ka nahin), to Chain Rule lagate hain:

blocks.text_alt: a equals d v of x by d t equals d v by d x times d x by d t

blocks.text: Lekin \(v = \frac{dx}{dt}\) hai, is liye humein milta hai:

blocks.text_alt: a equals v times d v by d x

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kaun sa formula kab lagana hai? Yeh exam mein bohat kaam ki baat hai:
1. \(v\) time \(t\) ka function diya ho: \(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\).
2. \(x\) time \(t\) ka function diya ho: do dafa differentiate karein, \(a = \frac{d^{2}x}{dt^{2}}\).
3. \(v\) displacement \(x\) ka function diya ho (sawal mein \(t\) nazar hi na aaye): \(a = v\frac{dv}{dx}\). Chain rule humein "\(x\) ke raaste" le jata hai, kyun ke \(v\) \(x\) par depend karta hai aur \(x\) \(t\) par.
Velocity aur acceleration ke signs ka khel bhi samajh lijiye: dono ka sign ek jaisa ho to particle tez ho raha hai (speeding up); signs ulte hon to particle aahista ho raha hai (slowing down). Jaise cycle par pedal maarna (velocity ki taraf zor) aur brake lagana (velocity ke ulat zor).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari misaal hai, kitab ki nahin.) Example 2 wala particle hi lijiye: \(v(t) = 3t^{2} - 12t\). Is ka acceleration:
\[a(t) = \dfrac{d}{dt}(3t^{2} - 12t)\]
\[= 6t - 12\]
\(t = 1\) par \(a(1) = 6 - 12 = -6\) m/s\(^{2}\). Ab dekhiye: \(t = 1\) par \(v = -9\) aur \(a = -6\), dono negative, yani ek hi sign. Is liye us lamhe particle negative direction mein tez ho raha hai.
Aur ek doosra sawal: \(v = 2x\) ho (velocity \(x\) ka function), to \(a = v\frac{dv}{dx} = 2x \cdot 2 = 4x\). Yahan \(\frac{dv}{dt}\) seedha nahin le sakte the, kyun ke \(v\) mein \(t\) hai hi nahin.
Units of Acceleration
Agar displacement meters mein aur time seconds mein naapa jaye, to acceleration ki unit meters per second square hai, yani m/s\(^{2}\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: "Per second square" kyun? Acceleration velocity (m/s) ki tabdeeli fi second hai: \(\frac{\text{m/s}}{\text{s}} = \text{m/s}^{2}\). Agar acceleration \(2\) m/s\(^{2}\) ho to iska matlab hai ke har second velocity \(2\) m/s barh jati hai: pehle second ke baad 2, doosre ke baad 4, teesre ke baad 6 m/s (agar shuru mein particle ruka hua tha).

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Seedhi line par direction sign se dikhate hain: ek taraf positive, doosri negative.
2. Average velocity \(= \frac{\text{total displacement}}{\text{total time}} = \frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}\); average speed \(= \frac{\text{total distance}}{\text{total time}}\).
3. Instantaneous velocity \(v = \frac{dx}{dt}\); instantaneous speed \(= |v|\).
4. Acceleration \(a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d^{2}x}{dt^{2}} = v\frac{dv}{dx}\); unit m/s\(^{2}\).
5. \(v\) aur \(a\) ka sign ek jaisa: tez ho raha hai; ulta: aahista ho raha hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Average velocity mein kul distance laga dena (ya average speed mein displacement). Sawal ka lafz ghor se parhein: velocity hai ya speed?
2. Average speed ko do speeds ka average samajh lena. Example 1 mein speeds 50 aur 60 m/min hain, magar average speed \(\frac{160}{3} \approx 53.3\) hai, 55 nahin. Hamesha kul distance ko kul time se divide karein.
3. Speed ko negative likhna: speed \(|v|\) hai, kabhi negative nahin.
4. Velocity ka minus sign gira dena: \(-9\) m/s aur \(9\) m/s mukhtalif jawab hain.
5. Jab \(v\) \(x\) ka function ho tab bhi \(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\) lagane ki koshish karna; wahan \(a = v\frac{dv}{dx}\) lagta hai.
